learning_outcomes: Explain api routes and request validation and how it connects to building a backend for ai applications.

content.intro: This lesson covers building a backend for ai applications through 6 syllabus subtopics preserved from the supplied Generative AI curriculum. Build API integrations with server-side secrets, input validation, safe retries, cancellation, observability, and budget controls. Model-provider payloads are not interchangeable by default.
content.why_it_matters: API routes and request validation belongs to the application integration boundary. Validate inputs before sending them, keep credentials on the server, handle non-success responses and cancellation, and log request metadata without storing secrets or unnecessary personal content. Provider-specific payloads must be checked against the selected API's current documentation.

items.title: Authentication and authorization
items.text: Authentication and authorization is a control problem as much as a model-behavior problem. Establish explicit boundaries in trusted application code, minimize data exposure, test realistic misuse and failure cases, and record who is responsible for reviewing residual risk. A prompt alone is not a security boundary.

content_blocks.title: Provider and version note
content_blocks.text: Model names, API payloads, supported modalities, quotas, pricing, and SDK behavior vary by provider and change over time. Treat linked official documentation as the authority for a live integration; examples here avoid hard-coded production model IDs and secrets.

content.task: Practice api routes and request validation within building a backend for ai applications: use a small synthetic input, predict the result, run the example, then change one input to test an edge case. Record the expected result and one limitation.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example uses a clearly described, non-sensitive input.
Expected behavior and at least one edge/failure case are written down.
The learner checks the result against an explicit criterion and records limitations.
hints: Begin with a tiny input whose expected behavior you can explain before running it.
Change one variable at a time and retain a fixed baseline for comparison.
When a model or external service is involved, inspect evidence and errors; do not treat the model response as a trusted instruction.

common_mistakes.mistake: Assuming fluent or plausible output is necessarily correct.
common_mistakes.fix: Use evidence, schema checks, representative test cases, and human review for consequential results.

common_mistakes.mistake: Changing several inputs or parameters at once.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep a baseline and vary one factor at a time so the effect can be interpreted.

common_mistakes.mistake: Putting secrets or private source material in prompts, logs, or a public example.
common_mistakes.fix: Use synthetic data, server-side secret storage, data minimization, and reviewed retention rules.
